A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. All 16 pages of v3 and 24 pages of v4, including appendices, are readable and comparable. The original experiments, tables, and eight figures can be matched despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original maze-solving experiments comparing solution-only, correct-trace, and swapped-trace training, together with GRPO results, generalization tests, and trace-validity analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds initialization and shuffling seed experiments, error analyses, and pretrained Qwen3-8B fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: The core trace-swapping and GRPO procedures remain. Appendix A.6 adds an adaptation using LoRA fine-tuning of pretrained Qwen3-8B, structured natural-language A* traces, and a corresponding trace validator.

E1.justification: The five principal maze families remain. V4 additionally evaluates a natural-language presentation of the maze task and summarizes a 100-instance obstacle-free 'no-maze' evaluation in Section 7, explicitly attributed to the companion work by Palod et al. (2025).

E2.justification: Table 10 adds a directly prompted, unfine-tuned Qwen3-8B-base comparator alongside the retained solution-only, correct-trace, and swapped-trace training regimes. The comparator membership in the original experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A.6 introduces a distinct pretrained-model protocol using natural-language traces, LoRA, and 25k fine-tuning steps. Appendix A.1 also revises reported training budgets from 95k/255k to 100k/250k steps for the 50k/500k datasets. The latter conflicts with Section 6.1's retained 255k statement; the PDFs do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendices A.2–A.3 test sensitivity to initialization and trace-shuffling seeds. A.4.1 adds first-error breakdowns for normal/swapped models and across GRPO checkpoints, while A.6 tests applicability to pretrained models. The original length-generalization and partial-swapping analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V4 reports additional initialization and shuffling seed runs and introduces Pearson/Spearman correlations with p-values for the trace-length analyses in Section 7. These substantially expand statistical reporting beyond v3's fixed-seed disclosure and existing five-run Searchformer averages; confidence intervals for the main accuracy comparisons remain absent.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5, the original figure results, and v3 Table 6, now Table 11, retain their numerical content. V4 adds seed results, error breakdowns, correlation statistics, and Table 10. In the new Qwen3-8B setting, correct traces outperform swapped traces across all five maze families, including 99.3% versus 76.6% plan accuracy on DFS.

T1.justification: The A* definitions, heuristic assumptions, and prompt-augmentation probability inequality and function are retained. V4 frames prompt augmentation more cautiously, but adds no substantive mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the main empirical claims. Section 8.1 explicitly qualifies the position: intermediate tokens need not have interpretable meaning, rather than being incapable of having it. This narrows the earlier categorical conclusion about end-user semantics.

C2.justification: Section 8.1 substantially expands implications for safety monitoring and recommends third-party verification. It develops the speculation that intermediate tokens move inputs closer to the training distribution. Appendix A.6 adds limitations concerning unknown pretraining and possible prior maze exposure, while A.4.1 interprets newly reported trace–plan mismatches and other failure modes.

D1.justification: V4 adds project and code links where v3 only promised release. Appendix A.6 supplies LoRA target layers, rank/scaling, optimizer settings, training details, and concrete prompt/trace examples. The expanded verifier description also explicitly documents wall-exploration and trace–plan-mismatch error categories.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive positioning against Neural Algorithmic Reasoning, including GNN and CLRS-related work, and scopes the novelty claim to autoregressive transformers. Additional references connect the study to trace evaluation, problem complexity, prompt augmentation, and safety-verification arguments.

P1.justification: Most main-text wording and section order remain. V4 locally expands the introduction and evaluation explanations, reorganizes the conclusion into 'Conclusion and Implications' with Section 8.1, expands the appendix structure, fixes the '[TO DO]' figure references, and updates author ordering and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively reformatted into the TMLR template, changing the author block, typography, spacing, and placement of material. Five appendix tables are added, and the former Table 6 becomes Table 11. All eight original figure graphics remain unchanged, although Figure 2's caption is expanded.

improvement.justification: V4 improves evidential transparency through seed controls and error analyses absent from v3, quantified correlations, and documented pretrained-model experiments. Its qualification about interpretable semantics also improves precision. These gains are limited by Section 6's overly broad 'largely consistent' description of Table 10, where correct traces outperform swapped traces throughout, and the conflicting 250k/255k training-budget statements.
